[2026-09-29, over four turns, answering CC's proposal that `cairn question open` search answered questions first]

'cairn question ask <question>' can use graph trees with failover to llm node deposit to look at everything we have and try and answer your question, and if it can't, then it fails over to tell you that it's run 'cairn question operator <question>' which goes into the operator inbox. So we literally use our own learning blocks to cache the answers and it gives you one path for questions. What do you think?

almost. every question is not a learning block. a learning block contains the questions and answers. the chart skill interacts with several, one for each phase. one way to think of a learning block is 'it's a constraining question nexus that takes an input, add from stored data, selects from the results, and then produces an output. two internal loops to evaluate that.' and so we'd have one or more of those in a line to process your questions. :) this is by the way a librarian function. to answer questions. about the code, about the intentions, whatever... and to learn as it goes. perhaps we've reached the place where that's the thing to do? build it out as a librarian function? 'cairn librarian ask <question>'?

almost... verbatim... that's not the point. quoting me is fine, but you might phrase a question differently (see the comments about syntactically equivalent earlier) that's why the graph trees. that will help us get equivalent questions answered with the same answer :) and if something not clear enough, then you can ask follow on questions, and the system keeps learning.

cairn librarian ask first is absolutely perfect
